summary.text: An air mass is a huge volume of air, covering hundreds or thousands of square miles, that is defined by its temperature and humidity.
Air masses take on the traits of the surface below them and are classified by latitude and by whether their source region is land or sea.
Weather fronts are the boundaries between air masses of different temperature or moisture, and once an air mass leaves its source region, the plants and water beneath it can quickly change it.

facts.label: Typical size
facts.value: Hundreds or thousands of square miles

facts.label: Code example
facts.value: cPk: continental polar, colder than the surface

facts.label: Main cT source
facts.value: The Sahara Desert in northern Africa

facts.label: Coldest type
facts.value: Arctic air, colder than polar air

items.prompt: A weather map labels an incoming body of air "mT". Where did it most likely take shape?
items.explain: "m" means maritime, so it formed over water and is moist, and "T" means tropical, so it formed in warm low latitudes.

items.prompt: Air builds up over northern Siberia in winter, far from any ocean and very cold. Which code fits it?
items.explain: "c" marks dry air from over land and "A" marks Arctic air, and Siberian winter air is given as an example of cA.

items.prompt: A chilly polar air mass streams out over the warm water of the Gulf Stream. Which stability letter is added to its code?

options.label: k, since the air is colder than the water under it
w, since the water is heating the air above it
m, since the air is now over the ocean
S, since the air is sinking and drying out

items.explain: The third letter compares the air with the surface below: "k" means the air is colder than that surface, and this case is written cPk.

items.prompt: Tropical air masses tend to come with lower air pressure than cold ones. What explains that?

options.label: They hold far less water vapour
They form high up in the mountains
Hot air rises while cold air sinks
The Earth spins slower near the poles

items.explain: Hot air rises and cold air sinks, which is why tropical air masses have lower pressure.

items.prompt: A stable polar air mass drifts over warmer ocean water and soaks up moisture. What happens to its stability?

options.label: It stays exactly as it was

items.explain: Polar air over the ocean loses its stability as it gains moisture over warmer water.

items.prompt: Continental tropical air is extremely hot and dry. Which place is the major source of it?
items.explain: This air forms over large low-latitude deserts, and the Sahara in northern Africa is its major source.
